def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain, non-empty file name: no separators, no "." or "..", no NUL, no drive or absolute form."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("..") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/b") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == ":" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if it is missing or unreadable.
    The name is untrusted. Any name that is not a safe plain file name gives ""."""
    post is_safe_name(name) or out == ""
    if not is_safe_name(name):
        return ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        return fs.read(name) else ""
